claim: Coiled coils are the best-understood protein fold, as their backbone structure can uniquely be described by parametric equations.
source: Coiled coils are the best-understood protein fold, as their backbone structure can uniquely be described by parametric equations.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Crick's work (Crick, 1953a) which established parametric equations for coiled coils, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: The insertion of two or six residues into the underlying heptad repeat of a parallel, trimeric coiled coil causes the local formation of short β-strands.
source: These insertions strain the supercoil to the breaking point, causing the local formation of short β-strands, which move the path of the chain by 120° around the trimer axis.
evidence: This is the primary experimental finding of the manuscript, supported by crystal structures presented in the results section.

claim: β-strands formed by insertions of two or six residues move the path of the chain by 120° around the trimer axis.
source: These insertions strain the supercoil to the breaking point, causing the local formation of short β-strands, which move the path of the chain by 120° around the trimer axis.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structures presented in the manuscript.

claim: The α/β coiled coil retains only one backbone hydrogen bond per repeat unit from the parent coiled coil.
source: The result is an α/β coiled coil, which retains only one backbone hydrogen bond per repeat unit from the parent coiled coil.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structures analyzed in the manuscript.

claim: α-Helical coiled coils are ubiquitous protein domains, found in a wide range of structural and functional contexts.
source: α-Helical coiled coils are ubiquitous protein domains, found in a wide range of structural and functional contexts (Lupas, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Coiled coils were the first protein fold described in atomic detail.
source: They were the first protein fold described in atomic detail (Crick, 1953b)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Crick's seminal work and represents historical scientific knowledge.

claim: Coiled coils are the only protein fold whose backbone structure can be computed with parametric equations.
source: and are also the only one whose backbone structure can be computed with parametric equations (Crick, 1953a)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Crick's work and represents established knowledge.

claim: Coiled coils consist of at least two α-helices, wound into superhelical bundles and held together by a mostly hydrophobic core.
source: They consist of at least two α-helices, wound into superhelical bundles and held together by a mostly hydrophobic core.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about coiled coils.

claim: In their most prevalent form, coiled coils follow a heptad sequence repeat pattern.
source: In their most prevalent form they follow a heptad sequence repeat pattern.
evidence: This is established knowledge about coiled coil structure.

claim: The seven positions in a heptad are labeled a – g, where positions a and d are oriented towards the core of the bundle and are thus mostly hydrophobic.
source: The seven positions in a heptad are labeled a – g, where positions a and d are oriented towards the core of the bundle and are thus mostly hydrophobic.
evidence: This is standard nomenclature and structural knowledge about coiled coils.

claim: An ideal, straight α-helix has a periodicity of about 3.63 residues per turn.
source: As an ideal, straight α-helix has a periodicity of about 3.63 residues per turn, the heptad coiled coil has a left-handed twist to reduce the periodicity to 3.5 residues per turn with respect to the bundle axis.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about α-helices.

claim: The heptad coiled coil has a left-handed twist to reduce the periodicity to 3.5 residues per turn with respect to the bundle axis.
source: As an ideal, straight α-helix has a periodicity of about 3.63 residues per turn, the heptad coiled coil has a left-handed twist to reduce the periodicity to 3.5 residues per turn with respect to the bundle axis.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about heptad coiled coils.

claim: Hendecad coiled coils are slightly right-handed.
source: In hendecad coiled coils, the situation is reversed: 11 residues are accommodated in 3 helical turns, resulting in 11/3 = 3.67 residues per turn. As this is slightly above 3.63, hendecads are slightly right-handed.
evidence: This is inferred from the mathematical relationship between periodicity and handedness.

claim: Right-handedness is as pronounced in pentadecad coiled coils as left-handedness is in heptad coiled coils.
source: With the periodicity of pentadecad coiled coils, 15/4 = 3.75 residues per turn, right-handedness is as pronounced as left-handedness is in heptad coiled coils.
evidence: This is inferred from the mathematical relationship between periodicity and handedness.

claim: Many naturally occurring coiled coils contain transitions between segments of different periodicity.
source: Many naturally occurring coiled coils contain transitions between segments of different periodicity (Alvarez et al., 2010; Hartmann et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Many naturally occurring coiled coils harbor discontinuities that retain the α-helical structure, but perturb the periodicity locally.
source: or harbor discontinuities that retain the α-helical structure, but perturb the periodicity locally (Parry, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The insertion of 3 residues is termed a stammer.
source: The insertion of 3 residues is termed a stammer, the insertion of 4 residues a stutter.
evidence: This is established nomenclature in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The insertion of 4 residues is termed a stutter.
source: The insertion of 3 residues is termed a stammer, the insertion of 4 residues a stutter.
evidence: This is established nomenclature in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Stammers lead to a local decrease in periodicity and an increase of left-handedness.
source: With 3 residues being less than one full turn of a helix, stammers lead to a local decrease in periodicity and an increase of left-handedness.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural properties of α-helices and coiled coils.

claim: Stutters have the opposite effect to stammers on periodicity and handedness.
source: Stutters have the opposite effect.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural properties of α-helices and coiled coils.

claim: A stutter inserted into a heptad coiled coil can locally extend one heptad to form a hendecad.
source: Inserted into a heptad coiled coil, a stutter can locally extend one heptad to form a hendecad (7 + 4 = 11 -> 11/3)
evidence: This is inferred from the mathematical relationship between insertions and periodicity.

claim: The insertion of 3 residues into a heptad coiled coil was predicted to cause an overwinding of the helices.
source: The insertion of a stammer into a heptad coiled coil, leading locally to a periodicity of 10/3 = 3.33, was predicted to cause an overwinding of the helices (Brown et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The structure of a stammer showed that the local overwinding introduced sufficient strain to cause the formation of a short 310-helical segment.
source: We could verify this experimentally: the structure of a stammer showed that the local overwinding introduced sufficient strain to cause the formation of a short 310-helical segment (Hartmann et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior experimental work by the authors.

claim: 3.33 (10/3) residues per turn mark the lower limit for periodicities in coiled coils.
source: We therefore assume that 3.33 (10/3) residues per turn mark the lower limit for periodicities.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observation of 310-helix formation at this periodicity.

claim: The upper limit for coiled coil periodicity is expected to be about 3.9 residues per turn.
source: As this is about 0.3 residues per turn less than the periodicity of a perfectly straight helix, one might expect the upper limit at a periodicity of about 3.9.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on symmetry with the lower limit.

claim: The vast majority of known coiled-coil structures deviating from the heptad repeat have periodicities higher than 3.5.
source: In fact the vast majority of known coiled-coil structures deviating from the heptad repeat have periodicities higher than 3.5
evidence: This is an observation from structural database analysis.

claim: The most extreme example of coiled coil periodicity is found in the trimeric autotransporter YadA, which has a local periodicity of 3.8 (19/5).
source: and the most extreme example is found in the trimeric autotransporter YadA, which has a local periodicity of 3.8 (19/5) (Alvarez et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Insertions of 1 or 5 residues have to be delocalized over at least two heptads to retain α-helical structure.
source: To retain α-helical structure, both insertions of 1 and 5 residues have to be delocalized over at least two heptads, leading to periodicities of 3.75 (15/4) and 3.8 (19/5), respectively.
evidence: This is inferred from the constraints on accessible periodicities shown in Figure 1.

claim: Insertions of 1 residue (skip residues) can be accommodated by the local formation of a π-turn in the α-helix.
source: Alternatively, insertions of 1 residue (skip residues) can be accommodated by the local formation of a π-turn in the α-helix, leaving the remaining coiled coil largely unperturbed (Lupas, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Insertions of 2 and 6 residues break the α-helices to form short β-strands.
source: We find that they indeed break the α-helices to form short β-strands, which associate into a triangular supersecondary structure we name the β-layer.
evidence: This is the primary experimental finding of the manuscript, supported by crystal structures.

claim: β-Layers are found repetitively in natural coiled coils, where they form regular fibers with alternating α- and β-structure.
source: β-Layers are found, also repetitively, in natural coiled coils, where they form regular fibers with alternating α- and β-structure, a protein fold that has not been described so far.
evidence: This is supported by the identification of β-layers in natural proteins and the crystal structure of Tcar0761.

claim: The α/β coiled coil is a protein fold that has not been described before.
source: β-Layers are found, also repetitively, in natural coiled coils, where they form regular fibers with alternating α- and β-structure, a protein fold that has not been described so far.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding, based on literature knowledge.

claim: OMP100 is a putative TAA in Actinobacillus actinomycetemcomitans that carries insertions of 2 and of 3 residues within the heptad repeats of its stalk.
source: As part of that study, we identified a putative TAA in Actinobacillus actinomycetemcomitans, OMP100, which carries insertions of 2 and of 3 residues within the heptad repeats of its stalk.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of the protein.

claim: The OMP100 construct yielded a typical α-helical CD spectrum.
source: The construct yielded a typical α-helical CD spectrum
evidence: This is experimental data from circular dichroism spectroscopy.

claim: The OMP100 construct unfolded cooperatively with a transition midpoint at 91°C upon heating.
source: and, upon heating, unfolded cooperatively with a transition midpoint at 91°C.
evidence: This is experimental data from thermal denaturation studies.

claim: Crystals of the OMP100 construct diffracted to a resolution of 2.3 Å.
source: We obtained crystals in space group C2 that diffracted to a resolution of 2.3 Å, with one symmetric trimer in the asymmetric unit.
evidence: This is experimental data from X-ray crystallography.

claim: The OMP100 structure showed a continuous heptad coiled coil with two discontinuities.
source: The structure showed a continuous heptad coiled coil with two discontinuities (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The insertion of 3 residues C-terminal to the N@d layers in OMP100 led to the formation of a decad, with a short 310-helical segment.
source: As expected, the insertion of 3 residues C-terminal to the N@d layers led to the formation of a decad, with a short 310-helical segment, as for the stammer we had described previously (Hartmann et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure, consistent with prior work.

claim: The insertion of 2 residues in OMP100 led to a sharp break in the coiled coil where the three chains of the trimer cross each other to form a triangular plane perpendicular to the coiled-coil axis.
source: However, the insertion of 2 residues led to a sharp break in the coiled coil: In the middle of the IENKADKAD motif, the three chains of the trimer cross each other to form a triangular plane perpendicular to the coiled-coil axis.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: Only the central three residues of the IENKADKAD motif (KAD) deviate from α-helical structure in OMP100.
source: Thereby only the central three residues of the motif, KAD, deviate from α-helical structure (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: All three residues of the β-layer in OMP100 fall into the β region of the Ramachandran plot.
source: All three fall into the β region of the Ramachandran plot, but only the central residue, alanine, forms backbone hydrogen bonds with the alanine residues of the other chains.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Only the central residue (alanine) of the β-layer in OMP100 forms backbone hydrogen bonds with the alanine residues of the other chains.
source: All three fall into the β region of the Ramachandran plot, but only the central residue, alanine, forms backbone hydrogen bonds with the alanine residues of the other chains.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The β-layer in OMP100 is essentially the same as the β-layer described as an adaptor between α-helical and β-stranded segments of TAAs.
source: It is essentially the same β-layer we described as an adaptor between α-helical and β-stranded segments of TAAs (Hartmann et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison with prior work.

claim: The β-layer in OMP100 directly connects two α-helical segments, where the C-terminal one is rotated counterclockwise by ~120° around the trimer axis.
source: Here it directly connects two α-helical segments, where the C-terminal one is rotated counterclockwise by ~120° around the trimer axis, as viewed from the N-terminus (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The two α-helical segments flanking the β-layer in OMP100 are stabilized in their relative orientation by backbone hydrogen bonds from the last residue of each N-terminal helix to the first residue in the C-terminal helix of the neighboring chain.
source: The two segments are stabilized in their relative orientation by backbone hydrogen bonds from the last (c position) residue of each N-terminal helix to the first (e position) residue in the C-terminal helix of the neighboring chain (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The backbone hydrogen bonds between flanking helices extend the continuous backbone hydrogen-bond network of each α-helix across the chains.
source: This extends the continuous backbone hydrogen-bond network of each α-helix across the chains.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observation of the hydrogen bonding pattern.

claim: The nature of the discontinuity represented by the β-layer is related to the nature of stammers, but its effects are much stronger.
source: The nature of the discontinuity represented by this β-layer is related to the nature of stammers, but its effects are much stronger.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of structural effects.

claim: The β-layer in OMP100 occurs in a motif of nine residues, a nonad.
source: While these stammers can be best described to be part of a decad, the β-layer in OMP100 occurs in a motif of nine residues, a nonad.
evidence: This is based on structural and sequence analysis.

claim: The requirements of a nonad on its helices would be even more extreme than those of a decad.
source: As the requirements of a nonad on its helices would be even more extreme than those of a decad, the strategy for its accommodation is a local but complete departure from helical structure.
evidence: This is inferred from the geometric constraints of coiled coils.

claim: All five GCN4 fusion constructs (A6, A7, A9, T6, T9) were resistant to proteolysis by proteinase K.
source: All five constructs were resistant to proteolysis by proteinase K, showed typical α-helical CD spectra, did not melt upon heating to 95°C and yielded well-diffracting crystals.
evidence: This is experimental data from proteolysis assays.

claim: All five GCN4 fusion constructs showed typical α-helical CD spectra.
source: All five constructs were resistant to proteolysis by proteinase K, showed typical α-helical CD spectra, did not melt upon heating to 95°C and yielded well-diffracting crystals.
evidence: This is experimental data from circular dichroism spectroscopy.

claim: All five GCN4 fusion constructs did not melt upon heating to 95°C.
source: All five constructs were resistant to proteolysis by proteinase K, showed typical α-helical CD spectra, did not melt upon heating to 95°C and yielded well-diffracting crystals.
evidence: This is experimental data from thermal denaturation studies.

claim: All five GCN4 fusion constructs yielded well-diffracting crystals.
source: All five constructs were resistant to proteolysis by proteinase K, showed typical α-helical CD spectra, did not melt upon heating to 95°C and yielded well-diffracting crystals.
evidence: This is experimental data from crystallization trials.

claim: The structures of all GCN4 fusion constructs were trimeric.
source: The structures of all constructs were trimeric and could be solved by molecular replacement, using the trimeric GCN4 structure as a search model.
evidence: This is a structural observation from X-ray crystallography.

claim: For T9, two structures were solved in alternative conformations.
source: For T9, two structures were solved in alternative conformations (Figure 3).
evidence: This is experimental data from X-ray crystallography.

claim: Apart from A7, which carries a heptad insert, all GCN4 fusion structures formed β-layers.
source: Apart from A7, which carries a heptad insert, all structures formed β-layers.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structures.

claim: All β-layers in the GCN4 fusion constructs are identical in their structure.
source: These are identical in their structure (Figure 4), although they are not accommodated in the same way.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison of the crystal structures.

claim: In A9 and T99, the β-layers are formed as in Actinobacillus OMP100.
source: In A9 and in one of the T9 structures, T99, the β-layers are formed as in Actinobacillus OMP100.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison.

claim: In A9 and T99, the first three and last three residues of the insert are in heptad register with the flanking GCN4 adaptors and constitute positions a, b, c and e, f, g.
source: The first three and last three residues of the insert are in heptad register with the flanking GCN4 adaptors and therefore constitute positions a, b, c and e, f, g.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structures.

claim: In A9 and T99, the middle three residues form the β-layer in place of position d.
source: The middle three residues, KAD in A9, KDD in T99, form the β-layer in place of position d (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structures.

claim: The A6 structure follows the same principle as A9 and T99, with the first three residues of the insert in heptad register with the N-terminal GCN4-adaptor.
source: The A6 structure follows the same principle: again the first three residues of the insert are in heptad register with the N-terminal GCN4-adaptor, constituting positions a, b and c.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: In A6, the register of the C-terminal GCN4-adaptor is shifted at the junction to the insert, starting with position e instead of position a.
source: As a consequence, the register of the C-terminal GCN4-adaptor is shifted at the junction to the insert, starting with position e instead of position a.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: In A6, the register conflict is resolved by the formation of a hendecad.
source: This register conflict is resolved further downstream by the formation of a hendecad (highlighted in pink in Figure 3A and C), so that the second half of the C-terminal adaptor retains its original register.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The T6 structure shows a 'real' 6-residue element.
source: In contrast, the T6 structure shows a 'real' 6-residue element.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: In T6, the β-layer is formed by the first three residues of the insert, MAT.
source: Here, the β-layer is formed by the first three residues of the insert, MAT (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: In T6, the last three residues of the insert assume geometrically clear e, f and g positions.
source: The last three residues of the insert assume geometrically clear e, f and g positions and the C-terminal GCN4 adaptor follows in its native register, starting with an a position.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: In T6, a conflict with the native register of the N-terminal adaptor is avoided with a small 'twist' to the adaptor's last residue.
source: A conflict with the native register of the N-terminal adaptor is avoided with just a small 'twist' to the adaptor's last residue: The C-terminal leucine, natively occurring in position g, is rotated outward from the core of the bundle by about 15° so that its Crick angle is biased towards the angle of a c position.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The alternative T9 structure, T96, starts out in the same way as T6, forming the β-layer with the first three residues of the insert, MAT, after a g/c position.
source: Surprisingly, the alternative T9 structure, T96, starts out in the same way, forming the β-layer with the first three residues of the insert, MAT, after a g/c position.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: In T96, the last three residues of the insert are accommodated as a sharply localized stammer.
source: The last three residues of the insert are accommodated as a sharply localized stammer, before the C-terminal adaptor starts in position a (highlighted in pink in Figure 3A and D).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The two structures T6 and T96 show that 6-residue elements are accommodated as N-terminally shortened 9-residue elements.
source: Thus, the two structures T6 and T96 show that 6-residue elements are accommodated as N-terminally shortened 9-residue elements.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of the two structures.

claim: β-layers can occur after both c and g positions.
source: While β-layers seem to strictly dictate the downstream register to start with an e position, they can occur after both c and g positions.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations across multiple constructs.

claim: β-layers which occur as connectors between TAA domains prefer small, hydrophobic residues in their central position.
source: We had previously found that β-layers which occur as connectors between TAA domains prefer small, hydrophobic residues in their central position (Hartmann et al., 2012; Bassler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: The A9b construct crystallized in two alternative structures.
source: A9b in fact crystallized in two alternative structures (Figure 3), but in both the β-layer formed over the central glutamate.
evidence: This is experimental data from X-ray crystallography.

claim: In both A9b structures, the β-layer formed over the central glutamate.
source: A9b in fact crystallized in two alternative structures (Figure 3), but in both the β-layer formed over the central glutamate.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structures.

claim: The central glutamate in A9b was too large and polar to be accommodated without distortion.
source: Since this residue was indeed too large and polar to be accommodated without distortion, the first turns of the downstream helices are perturbed to different extents in both instances, leading to a pronounced kink in one of the structures (highlighted in pink in Figure 3A).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The Tcar0761 construct contains four consecutive β-layers.
source: It shows the anticipated α/β coiled coil with four consecutive β-layers.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The Tcar0761 structure was solved to a resolution of 1.6Å.
source: Crystallization trials yielded crystals in space group P63, diffracting to a resolution of 1.6Å, with one chain in the asymmetric unit and the trimer built by crystallographic symmetry around the c axis.
evidence: This is experimental data from X-ray crystallography.

claim: In Tcar0761, the β-layers are formed by the residues MAT of the repeats.
source: These layers are formed by the residues MAT of the repeats; the other residues, corresponding to KDDIAN, constitute positions e,f,g,a,b,c of the segments between the β-layers.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: In Tcar0761, the repeats can be written as IANMATKDD, with the isoleucine forming classical hydrophobic a layers and the MAT forming β-layers in place of position d.
source: Therefore, in accordance with heptad notation, the repeats can be written as IANMATKDD, with the isoleucine forming classical hydrophobic a layers and the MAT forming β-layers in place of position d (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: Only the first β-layer in Tcar0761 is part of a 6-residue element (hexad) and occurs after a position g of the preceding heptad.
source: Only the first β-layer is part of a 6-residue element (hexad) and occurs after a position g of the preceding heptad.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The α/β coiled coil is a new class of protein fiber, based on a novel supersecondary structure element.
source: With its alternating a- and β-layers, the α/β coiled coil is a new class of protein fiber, based on a novel supersecondary structure element.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural characterization of Tcar0761.

claim: The α/β coiled coil of Thermosinus Tcar0761 is built of nonads and contains six residues per repeat in the α region of the Ramachandran plot.
source: The α/β coiled coil of Thermosinus Tcar0761 is built of nonads and thus contains six residues per repeat in the α region of the Ramachandran plot, which retain one backbone hydrogen bond characteristic of α-helical structure.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: The α/β coiled coil of Tcar0761 retains one backbone hydrogen bond characteristic of α-helical structure per repeat.
source: The α/β coiled coil of Thermosinus Tcar0761 is built of nonads and thus contains six residues per repeat in the α region of the Ramachandran plot, which retain one backbone hydrogen bond characteristic of α-helical structure.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure.

claim: A minimalistic α/β coiled coil could be built of hexads, with three residues in the β and three in the α region of the Ramachandran plot.
source: We think that it should be possible to reduce this structure by removing three α-helical residues and thus the single remaining backbone hydrogen bond from the parent structure. Such a minimalistic α/β coiled coil would be built of hexads, with three residues in the β and three in the α region of the Ramachandran plot.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about a possible structure.

claim: A tail-fiber protein from a Streptococcus pyogenes prophage (2C3F) contains an α/β coiled coil with four β-layers, two of which are in a hexad spacing.
source: However, as we will show in the next section, a tail-fiber protein from a Streptococcus pyogenes prophage (2C3F) contains an α/β coiled coil with four β-layers, two of which are in a hexad spacing.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of an existing PDB structure.

claim: The β-layers in the DUF3782 family have the consensus sequence [aliphatic]–A–T–K–[polar]–[DE].
source: The β-layers in this family have the consensus sequence [aliphatic]–A–T–K–[polar]–[DE] (Figure 6).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of the protein family.

claim: A family of integral membrane proteins found in prokaryotes and mitochondria (DUF1640) carry the β-layer motif prominently at the beginning of their C-terminal stalk.
source: Pattern searches with this motif led us to the discovery of a family of integral membrane proteins found in prokaryotes and mitochondria (DUF1640), which carry this motif prominently at the beginning of their C-terminal stalk (Figure 6).
evidence: This is based on sequence pattern searches.

claim: All proteins with β-layers identified in the structural database are homotrimers, except for the SLH domain, which is a monomer with pseudo-threefold symmetry.
source: All proteins we identified are homotrimers, except for the SLH domain, which is a monomer with pseudo-threefold symmetry
evidence: This is based on analysis of protein structures in the PDB.

claim: A majority of proteins with β-layers are from viruses, mainly bacteriophage.
source: a majority are from viruses, mainly bacteriophage.
evidence: This is based on analysis of protein structures in the PDB.

claim: Most β-layers occur in the context of coiled coils.
source: Most β-layers occur in the context of coiled coils and we have termed these 'canonical'.
evidence: This is based on analysis of protein structures in the PDB.

claim: Canonical β-layers are usually found capping one of the ends of the coiled coil, more often the N-terminal than the C-terminal one.
source: They are usually found capping one of the ends of the coiled coil, more often the N-terminal than the C-terminal one
evidence: This is based on analysis of protein structures in the PDB.

claim: MPN010 contains a coiled coil with internal β-layers.
source: and we have found only two further examples of coiled coils with internal β-layers: MPN010, a protein of unknown function from Mycoplasma pneumoniae (2BA2), and the aforementioned tail-fiber protein with hyaluronidase activity from the Streptococcus pyogenes prophage SF370.1 (2C3F).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the PDB structure 2BA2.

claim: The tail-fiber protein from Streptococcus pyogenes prophage SF370.1 (2C3F) contains a coiled coil with four β-layers, one near the N-terminus, two internal, and one at the C-terminal end.
source: The latter contains a coiled coil with four β-layers, one near the N-terminus, two internal, and one at the C-terminal end
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the PDB structure 2C3F.

claim: The two internal β-layers in the Streptococcus prophage tail-fiber protein have the sequence LQQKADKETVYTKAE and are in a hexad spacing.
source: the two internal β-layers have the sequence LQQKADKETVYTKAE and are thus in a hexad spacing, with the first resembling the β-layer sequence of OMP100 and the second the one of Tcar0761.
evidence: This is based on structural and sequence analysis of the PDB structure 2C3F.

claim: The second internal β-layer in the Streptococcus prophage tail-fiber protein deviates from canonical β-layer structure.
source: Remarkably, this second β-layer deviates from canonical β-layer structure, which we attribute to the serine in the first core position of the downstream coiled coil.
evidence: This is a structural observation from analysis of the PDB structure 2C3F.

claim: Tandems with the consensus sequence LxxKADKxxVYTKxE occur in many bacterial ORFs.
source: Nevertheless, such tandems with the consensus sequence LxxKADKxxVYTKxE occur in many bacterial ORFs (also in some TAAs, such as Neisseria meningitidis NadA4) and thus probably constitute a co-optimized module.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of bacterial genomes.

claim: Canonical β-layers favor hydrophobic residues in β1 and β2 positions.
source: A structural analysis of canonical β-layers in light of their conserved sequence patterns (Figure 6, Table 2) shows that they favor hydrophobic residues in β1 and β2 (Figure 6)
evidence: This is based on sequence and structural analysis of β-layers.

claim: The β2 residue in canonical β-layers tends to be of smaller size (i.e. A or V).
source: and particularly the β2 residue tends to be of smaller size (i.e. A or V).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of β-layers.

claim: Canonical β-layers can follow upon either position a or d of the preceding coiled coil, but always lead into positions e, f, g of the following coiled coil.
source: They can follow upon either position a or d of the preceding coiled coil, but always lead into positions e, f, g of the following coiled coil.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of β-layers in multiple structures.

claim: When β-layers follow upon position a they yield the register a-b-c-β1-β2-β3-e-f-g (seen in nonads).
source: Thus, when they follow upon position a they yield the register a-b-c-β1-β2-β3-e-f-g (seen in nonads)
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of β-layers.

claim: When β-layers follow upon position d they bias the residue in position g towards c to yield the register e-f-g/c-β1-β2-β3-e-f-g (seen in hexads).
source: whereas when they follow upon position d they bias the residue in position g towards c to yield the register e-f-g/c-β1-β2-β3-e-f-g (seen in hexads).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of β-layers.

claim: For β-layers that occur at the N-terminal end of coiled coils, the β3 residue acts as an N-cap for the following helix, coordinating the backbone NH group of residue g.
source: For β-layers that occur at the N-terminal end (for example in the necks of TAAs or in influenza hemagglutinin HA2), the β3 residue acts as an N-cap for the following helix, coordinating the backbone NH group of residue g (Figure 8)
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of β-layers.

claim: The β3 residue in N-terminal β-layers is almost always D, N, T, or S.
source: it is thus almost always D, N, T, or S (the capping role of this residue has been described in detail in the fusion-pH structure of influenza hemagglutinin HA2 (Chen et al., 1999).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of β-layers and supported by citation.

claim: The sidechain of the residue in position g following an N-terminal β-layer forms a hydrogen bond with the backbone NH group of the β3 residue.
source: In return, the sidechain of the residue in position g forms a hydrogen bond with the backbone NH group of the β3 residue, closing a ring of sidechain-backbone interactions between these two residues
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of β-layers.

claim: The residue in position g following an N-terminal β-layer is almost always D, E, or Q.
source: it is thus almost always D, E, or Q.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of β-layers.

claim: The residue in position e following an N-terminal β-layer is broadly conserved as K or R.
source: Where it is D or E, it can further form a salt bridge to the residue in position e of the neighboring chain (clockwise as viewed from the N-terminus), which is broadly conserved as K or R.
evidence: This is based on sequence and structural analysis of β-layers.

claim: The residue in position e following an N-terminal β-layer essentially always forms either a salt bridge with the β3 residue or a hydrogen bond with the backbone carbonyl group of the β1 residue.
source: This residue essentially always forms either this salt bridge, or a hydrogen bond with the backbone carbonyl group of the β1 residue, as depicted in Figure 8.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of β-layers.

claim: β-layers that occur within coiled coils show substantially the same interactions and conservation patterns as the ones that act as N-caps, when the residue in β1 is hydrophobic.
source: β-Layers that occur within coiled coils show substantially the same interactions and conservation patterns as the ones that act as N-caps, when the residue in β1 is hydrophobic.
evidence: This is based on structural and sequence analysis of β-layers.

claim: When the β1 residue is K in internal β-layers, the interaction network changes entirely from an N-cap of the following helices to a C-cap of the preceding ones.
source: However, when the β1 residue is K (mainly in the stalks of TAAs and related phage proteins) the interaction network changes entirely from an N-cap of the following helices to a C-cap of the preceding ones.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of β-layers.

claim: In a tandem of β-layers with hexad spacing, the first layer should favor a C-capping network, with K in position β1, and the second an N-capping network, with a hydrophobic residue in β1.
source: These considerations suggest that in a tandem of β-layers with hexad spacing, the first layer should favor a C-capping network, with K in position β1, and the second an N-capping network, with a hydrophobic residue in β1.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis of β-layer interaction networks.

claim: The prediction about tandem β-layers is observed in the Streptococcus prophage tail-fiber protein (2C3F).
source: This is in fact observed in the Streptococcus prophage tail-fiber protein (2C3F).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the PDB structure 2C3F.

claim: The range of periodicities that α-helical coiled coils can assume is limited by the strain they impose on the constituent helices.
source: The range of periodicities that α-helical coiled coils can assume is limited by the strain they impose on the constituent helices, as they progressively deviate from the 3.63 residues per turn of an undistorted α-helix.
evidence: This is a general principle inferred from structural knowledge of coiled coils.

claim: Insertions of 3 residues into a heptad background (stammers, 10/3 = 3.33) lead to the largest strain observed so far in continuous coiled coils.
source: Insertions of 3 residues into a heptad background (stammers, 10/3 = 3.33) lead to the largest strain observed so far in continuous coiled coils and are accommodated by the local distortion of the α-helix into a 310 helix.
evidence: This is based on prior structural studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Increasing the strain further by insertions of 2x3 or 3x3 residues leads to a complete loss of helical structure and the local formation of short β-strands.
source: We find that increasing the strain further by insertions of 2x3 or 3x3 residues leads to a complete loss of helical structure and the local formation of short β-strands.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the manuscript, supported by crystal structures.

claim: β-layers offer two clear advantages to protein fibers: they increase their resilience by tightly interleaving the monomers within the fiber and they offer a simple mechanism to integrate β-stranded domains into these fibers.
source: We propose that β-layers offer two clear advantages to protein fibers. They increase their resilience by tightly interleaving the monomers within the fiber and they offer a simple mechanism to integrate β-stranded domains into these fibers, thus increasing their functional complexity.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the functional advantages of β-layers.

claim: A novel backbone structure is accessible to the 20 proteinogenic amino acids in the allowed regions of the Ramachandran plot with only minor mutations to a known fold.
source: Our results show that a novel backbone structure is accessible to the 20 proteinogenic amino acids in the allowed regions of the Ramachandran plot with only minor mutations to a known fold.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural findings of the manuscript.
